# Mod Loading

Make sure your mod only runs with CoE5SE, and load another mod's scripts before yours.

These go in the .c5m, with the game's own `icon`, `description` and `modprio`.

!!! info "More in the game's manual"
    `icon`, `description`, `modprio` and the game's other mod info commands are in Illwinter's official modding manual, under ["Mod Info"](https://www.illwinter.com/coe5/coe5modding.pdf#page=4).

### needs_glu32.dll_and_CoE5SE_enabled_at_launch { #needs-glu32-dll-and-coe5se-enabled-at-launch data-toc-label="needs_glu32.dll_and_CoE5SE_enabled_at_launch" }

Stops the game with its Mod Error when CoE5SE isn't running. Put it in every mod that needs CoE5SE: a Lua or DLL mod, or one with CoE5SE commands on plain .c5m lines. A mod whose CoE5SE lines are all in its .c5se or on `#!@` lines doesn't need it.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    needs_glu32.dll_and_CoE5SE_enabled_at_launch
    ```

### requires &lt;ModName&gt; { #requires data-toc-label="requires" }

Loads another mod's DLLs and Lua scripts before yours. To use its .c5m or .c5se content, give your mod a higher `modprio`. If that mod isn't enabled, your mod still loads without it. Write it on a plain .c5m line: CoE5SE doesn't read `#!@requires`.

- **ModName:** The other mod's .c5m file name without `.c5m`, capitals included.

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    requires MiddleEarth
    ```

### Example .c5m { #example }

=== ".c5m"

    ```c5m
    icon "banner.tga"
    description "The wizards, realms and peoples of Middle-earth. Needs CoE5SE."
    needs_glu32.dll_and_CoE5SE_enabled_at_launch
    requires MiddleEarth
    ```
